dataset.name: Soil Nitrogen, Water Content, Microbial Biomass, and Archaeal, Bacterial and Fungal Communities from the East River Watershed, Colorado collected in 2016-2017
description: This data set contains soil measurements made at the Pumphouse Hillslope to Floodplain transect at the locations of the early snowmelt-timing manipulation experiments in the East River Watershed in Colorado, USA. The data were collected in 2016 and 2017 to determine soil microbial responses to snow accumulation, snowmelt, and transition from winter to spring. Some additional data from the Washington Gulch snowmelt manipulation experiment lcoations are also included here.

Data were collected on soil cores collected in the field at three soil depths (0 to 5 cm, 5 to 15 cm, 15 cm +) below the soil surface and analyzed in the on homogenized samples with roots and gravel removed.

Data include gravimetric soil water content (48 hr oven-dried) and soil pH measurements (1:1 w/vol in ddH2O), dissolved nitrogen pools measured in soil extracts (2M KCl extractant), microbial biomass carbon and nitrogen (0.5M K2SO4 extractant), and archaeal, bacterial, and fungal species determined by Illumina 300 bp paired-read marker gene sequencing (16S rDNA for archaea and bacteria and ITS for fungi).

spatialCoverage.description: The East River (ER) is a snow‐dominated, headwater basin of the Upper Colorado River Basin (UCRB) located in the western United States. The ER is the designated testbed of Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory's Watershed Function Scientific Focus Area (WFSFA). Through WFSFA, observational networks have been established to measure stream discharge and precipitation chemistry.The ER is considered representative of many snow‐dominated headwaters of the Rocky Mountains. The study domain encompasses nearly 85 square km, a 1.4‐km vertical drop in elevation (4,120 to 2,760 m) and pristine alpine, subalpine, montane, and riparian ecosystems. The ER contains high‐energy mountain streams to low‐energy meandering floodplains and is eroding primarily into the Cretaceous, carbon‐rich, marine shale of the Mancos Formation.

measurementTechnique: Soil cores were collected using a 4-cm diameter bulk density corer and split in the field at three depth increments 0 to 5 cm, 5 to 15 cm, 15 cm +). An ~10 g subsample of each soil sample was immediately frozen on a dry ice in the field for microbial DNA analysis. The remainder was kept at 4 deg C for chemical analysis.

Gravimetric water content was measured as water lost during a 48 hr incubation at 60 deg C. Soil pH was measured in a 1:1 w/vol soil slurry in ddH2O. Total dissolved nitrogen was measured colorimetrically following persulfate digestion. Inorganic nitrogen pools (e.g., ammonium and nitrate) were measured in 2M KCl soil extracts using colorimetry. Microbial biomass carbon and nitrogen were measured using the chloroform fumigation extraction method followed by colorimetric determination of organic carbon or total nitrogen by colorimetry for carbon or nitrogen, respectively. Microbial community DNA was extracted from soil samples using the PowerSoil DNA extraction kit and marker genes sequenced using Illumina MiSeq v3 250 bp paired read sequencing.

This section provides a list of all source material physical samples used in this dataset, collected by using a soil bulk density corer attached to a slide hammer. More information describing the samples is provided in sample landing pages (links below), and the WatershedSFA_SoilCores_Metadata__2_.xls dataset file.
